key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model combining spectral, connectivity, and topological features improved subject-level ADHD classification, with SVM performing best.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests EEG-based machine learning may help support more objective ADHD biomarker research, but it is not ready to replace clinical diagnosis.
method: EEG from 121 subjects was preprocessed and split into overlapping windows.
Features were extracted from three domains: spectral, wPLI-based functional connectivity, and persistent-homology topology.
RFE selected 110 features, and five classifiers were tested with stratified five-fold cross-validation plus ablation and SHAP/LIME interpretation.
evidence_signal: The best model was SVM, reaching 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 80.14% balanced accuracy, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
watch_item: The dataset is relatively small, so performance may not generalize well without external validation on independent cohorts.
paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
